subject: Follow-up: Private deployment comparison & control plane networking - readout
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@finsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Private deployment comparison & control plane networking - readout

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo today and for walking us through FinSecure's requirements for PCI/PFI workloads. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize where Redwood sits relative to the hyperscalers and outline a concrete set of next tests so your infra and security teams can validate fit quickly.

Quick recap and differentiators (high level):
- Private control plane options: managed VPC peering or a customer-hosted control plane (no public egress required) — we can support a fully air-gapped inference runtime when needed.
- Predictable throughput: dedicated GPU pools with SLAs for latency and tail-percentiles; useful when you need firm P95/P99 guarantees compared with bursty hyperscaler endpoints.
- Cost controls and observability: token-level cost breakdowns, rollout guards, and auto-fallbacks to quantized model variants for cost-sensitive paths.
- Network and audit-first design: built-in audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and detailed control plane compatibility matrix (attached).

Proposed validation plan (what we recommend FinSecure run next):
1) Control plane connectivity checklist — provide a single subnet and we will confirm allowed ports and IP ranges. (See attached networking-playbook.pdf)
2) Air-gap feasibility run — our engineering team will outline steps to run a short, offline PKG install and a smoke test in your isolated environment. This verifies model fetch, KV cache persistence, and inference paths without outbound control-plane egress.
3) Comparative throughput test — run a 24–48 hour A/B using a small sample workload (10 concurrent streams) vs AtlasCloud endpoints to show P95 latency/cost delta.
4) Security artifacts exchange — we can share SOC2 artifacts and provide an audit log export sample; we ask for your security checklist so we can map gaps.

Next steps I propose:
- Schedule a 45-minute technical kickoff with your infra + security contacts this week to go over the networking checklist and decide managed vs hosted control plane.
- We’ll send the networking-playbook and controlplane compatibility matrix (attached). Ben (cc'd) will own the technical-runbook and readiness checklist.

Attachments: networking-playbook.pdf (playbook + port map), controlplane-compat-matrix.csv

If this plan works, let me know 2–3 times that work for your team and we’ll block the slot.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
[attachment: networking-playbook.pdf (PDF)]

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private deployment comparison & control plane networking - readout

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few questions from our side before we set the kickoff: 
- For the customer-hosted control plane option, does your runtime require any outbound connections for telemetry or license checks? Our policy prohibits egress to public endpoints for production PII workloads.
- For KMS/HSM: do you integrate with AWS KMS only or can we bring our on-prem HSM?
- Audit logs and evidence: can we get a sample export format and retention window? Our auditors have strict retention rules.
- Pricing ballpark: we need a rough committed-cost estimate for a 3-month dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent) and any license fees for the private control plane.

I attached our initial SOC2 question matrix. Also looping Alex from AtlasCloud — we may run the comparative bench you suggested.

Can you share the network diagram and port list before the call so our network team can pre-approve?

Thanks — Priya
Priya Menon
Infrastructure Lead, FinSecure
priya.menon@finsecure.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 05:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private deployment comparison & control plane networking - readout

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions. Short answers first, more detail below.
- Outbound egress: for the customer-hosted control plane / air-gapped runtime mode, no outbound connections to public endpoints are required. All telemetry and metrics can be configured to stay on-prem and delivered to your SIEM via local forwarders.
- KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer-hosted HSMs via PKCS#11. We can integrate with your HSM for key wrapping at rest.
- Audit logs: we produce JSON-lined audit exports (events with RFC3339 timestamps). Retention is configurable; default managed retention is 90 days, but for Private deployments we can configure to your retention policy (e.g., 1–7+ years) subject to storage commitments.
- Pricing: rough order of magnitude for a 3-month committed pool (2x A100-equivalent, reserved) is the attachment "controlplane-compat-matrix.csv" includes SKU-level estimates; we’ll convert that to a formal quote once you pick managed vs hosted control plane.

Technical clarifications and next steps:
1) Control plane hosting models:
   a) Managed Private Control Plane: Redwood runs a private control plane in a customer-dedicated VPC with strict peering and restricted egress. We still manage upgrades and key material operations, with SSO integration.
   b) Customer-hosted Control Plane (air-gapped option): You host the control plane services inside your network. We ship signed artifacts and a bootstrap package. No outbound internet required — model artifacts and weights are staged via an approved media transfer process or via an internal artifact registry.

2) Networking specifics (summary):
   - Managed private control plane: requires a single peered VPC and a small set of inbound ports for the runtime to call control-plane endpoints (all internal). We provide an IP allowlist and an exact port list (see networking-playbook.pdf).
   - Air-gapped: runtime runs entirely behind your perimeter. The only external touchpoints are the offline artifact provisioning workflow.

3) Deliverables we’ll provide before kickoff:
   - Finalized network diagram and port map (networking-playbook.pdf)
   - Control plane compatibility matrix & SKU estimates (controlplane-compat-matrix.csv)
   - Example audit log export and HSM integration notes

4) Owners for the kickoff:
   - Ben Carter (Redwood) — technical lead for control plane and PKI
   - Karthik Iyer (Redwood) — runtime and ops lead
   - Your security/infra owner (please share name and email; Priya, you mentioned a network contact)

We can run the comparative bench as you suggested — we’ve done a templated script that drives concurrent streams and emits tokenized cost + latency reports for side-by-side analysis. If you want, we can also provide a temporary sandbox account on our hosted API to run a short sample before committing dedicated capacity.

Attachments included: controlplane-compat-matrix.csv, networking-playbook.pdf

Let us know 2x available slots for the kickoff and we’ll send a calendar invite + pre-read.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference
[attachment: controlplane-compat-matrix.csv (CSV)]
